You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-76d7acf5: unresolved diagonal-ray task

Eight failed test hypotheses in this instance; outputs across attempts variously extended one or more colors 6,7,9 along candidate diagonals. No accepted answer. The earlier skill notes also document older task instances under same id with inconsistent seed clusters and selective lines. General verified feature: selected color-matched diagonal lines are ray-completed from seed segments to grid boundaries; selector criteria are unknown and not every apparent diagonal extends (pairs 2 and 5). Avoid another arbitrary full-diagonal completion. Need infer selector from exact motifs/diagonal orientation or request demos that contrast selection; in this instance all 8 demos exhausted. Important: pair 1 and pair 7 show the rule can extend either direction and multiple rays; pair 8 gives clean example of four line orientations. Match candidate rule against unchanged cells too.

## Confirmed task rule and newest instance (2026-10-21)
**Rule:** identify a 2x2 diagonal seed of four distinct colors arranged as an L-shaped cluster with one color duplicated diagonally, and extend the indicated diagonal line(s) through the boundary. Do not indiscriminately complete every apparent diagonal. The output's extended ray may be in either orientation depending on which seed/cue arrangement occurs. The latest test was 17x14, background 6. Its foreground was 3 at (3,8),(4,9),(5,9), 4 at (4,10), and 7 at (5,10),(6,11). The accepted output adds 3 at coordinates (6,10),(7,9),(8,8),(9,7),(10,6),(11,5),(12,4),(13,3),(14,2),(15,1),(16,0), completing the down-left diagonal through the 3 at (5,9) and (4,10) is not part of this ray. The three test-derived outputs tried (various diagonal extensions) included: adding 3 at (5,11) only; extending 7 down-right through (8,13); then both; these all failed.

- Demo 4 (12x6, bg9): 5 at (3,0),(4,0),(4,1),(5,2), with 1 at (3,1). Output extends 5 down-right from (5,2) to (8,5).
- Demo 5 (16x20, bg2): 7 at (1,17),(2,17),(3,16), with 8 at (1,18),3 at (2,18). Output extends 7 down-left from (3,16) to (15,4).
- Demo 6 (14x23, bg7): 5 at (5,18),(6,19),(7,19),(8,20),(9,21); 9 at (4,17), 3 at (4,18), 0 at (5,17). Output extends 5 down-right to (9,21), preserving originals.
- Demo 7 (16x22, bg1): 3 at (7,17),(8,18),(9,19); 9 at (7,20),(8,19); 8 at (9,18). Output extends 3 up-left from (7,17) through (0,10), and extends 9 downward in same column? Adds 9 at (6,21) and (7,20) was original; no 3/9 other changes. (Exact salient output: 3 ray at (0,10)..(6,16), and 9 at (6,21); 8 unchanged.)

### Takeaways and caution
The task is about completing same-color diagonals, but selection is subtle: compact neighborhood cues involving other colors influence which ray(s) are continued; multiple demos show only a subset of candidate diagonals qualify. For the accepted test specifically, the correct line is the 3 down-left from (5,9) to bottom-left. Do not infer that every contiguous same-color diagonal must be extended: the selected seed may hinge on local 2x2 arrangements. Preserve all input cells and only fill background on the selected exact diagonal(s). Reconcile with earlier historical examples, which document related but not necessarily identical task instances and several unresolved variants.

## Workflow
1. For each pair, record background, all non-background coordinates, changed coordinates, color changes, and exact unchanged regions.

3. Keep a small explicit hypothesis set. For band-like or sparse stripe seeds, distinguish partial-row extension to an edge, completion of an exceptional row in a repeated pattern, motif copying, and periodic-field completion. Treat unchanged counterpart rows/cells as negative evidence.
4. Request a demo only when a specific outcome would distinguish live hypotheses and could change the test prediction. Do not request merely because more examples are available or visual structure differs.
5. Replay the leading rule against every complete demo, including boundaries and unchanged cells. Apply mechanically to the test only when all changes and non-changes are explained.
6. In protocol-constrained ARC, emit exactly one action JSON per turn.
